note: Adapted from the English species-level description in Bacchus (1997); the alate is recorded as Unknown in the original, so the soldier section is taken here; measurements are taken from the rows of the measurement table whose labels and values correspond directly.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and labrum yellow; mandibles brown to reddish brown with yellow bases; postmentum concolorous with the head, slightly darker than the genae; antennae, thoracic nota, abdomen and legs pale yellow. Head capsule short-oval, slightly longer than wide, posterior margin broadly and evenly rounded; sides of head with numerous short to a few long setae, dorsal setae numerous and of unequal length, arranged symmetrically. Labrum ligulate, apex pointed, with 8 setae on the anterior third, the apical pair longest. Mandibles moderately slender, apex weakly to moderately incurved, curvature 0.03—0.05 mm. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segment 4 slightly longer than segment 3, segments 1 and 2 subequal. Postmentum short and broad. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin with a deep V-shaped notch, posterior margin slightly concave, lateral lobes with a few long setae. Fore tibia moderately inflated; fore tibial spurs 3, the dorsal spur as long as the outer ventral spur; the long seta on the coxa not spine-like. Measurements (26 heads, 13 colonies): head length (including mandibles) 1.20—1.35 mm (type 1.28 mm); head length to mandible base 0.78—0.90 mm; head width behind the antennal sockets 0.63—0.70 mm; maximum head width 0.68—0.75 mm; labrum length 0.28—0.30 mm; maximum labrum width 0.18—0.20 mm; left mandible length 0.48—0.50 mm.
